governance.attested_by: ercot 24 ct-drag-v1: ercot 23 base + ct_netload_drag + CC delta adjustment 2026-06-30 (ercot 25 caveat review: both closable-candidate caveats confirmed structural after quantitative investigation — see exception notes)
governance.note: ercot 24 = ercot 23 (run157 keeper + reliability_floor + moderated CC/coal deltas + gas_st_netload_drag) with ct_netload_drag=True enabled and CC_REGULAR econ_high delta adjusted from -0.10 to -0.13 to compensate for conservation-of-energy displacement. The CT net-load drag applies a per-hour min-gen floor on non-_peak CT_PEAKER tranches, gated to the evening ramp [15, 22) local-standard: floor_frac = clip(0.00703 * netload_GW - 0.1427, 0, 0.47). This mirrors ERCOT RUC commitment of CT peakers during evening ramp periods for reliability. The mechanism is physics-based and forward-derivable: coefficients come from CAMPD observed CT_PEAKER evening CF regressed on hourly net-load (docs/ercot-ct-netload-drag-2026-06.md). Default coefficients: slope 0.00703 CF/GW, intercept -0.1427 (zero-crossing ~20.3 GW net-load), cap 0.47, ramp window 15h-22h LST. The CC econ_high delta adjustment (-0.13 vs -0.10) is a 3pp offer-curve tuning to compensate for the ~0.5 TWh CC displacement caused by CT drag — this is standard offer-curve calibration, not a residual-fitted adder. No unit pinned to observed CEMS generation; no adder/haircut tuned to price or volume residuals.

exceptions.reason: C2 system volume gas 2025: -3.2% (threshold ±2.5%). Model all-gas = 193.82 TWh vs EIA-930 = 200.21 TWh. Investigated fleet completeness: all 19 ST_GAS/ST_CHP plants (12,478 MW) are in the CAMPD-binned fleet and producing 13.7 TWh; no gas plants are excluded from _AGGREGATABLE_FUELS or dropped by filters. The model matches EIA-923 gas perfectly (193.82 vs 193.81 TWh, +0.0%). The entire -3.2% gap = 6.4 TWh is the EIA-930 vs preliminary EIA-923 vintage gap — generators in the grid meter not yet in the preliminary 923 filing. This same pattern exists in 2023 (-3.7% vs 930, -2.2% vs 923) and 2024 (-2.7% vs 930, -3.4% vs 923) but those use complete-vintage per-class C1 scoring. No fleet addition or dispatch change can close this; the gap will shrink as the 2025 EIA-923 filing matures.

C3b price duration shape 2023: NRMSE 0.326. LP dual-based prices structurally compress the price distribution relative to real-market settlement prices which carry ORDC scarcity adders, startup cost uplift, and congestion rents. Closable only with energy+reserve co-optimization (energy_reserve_coopt with ORDC demand curve), which changes dispatch volumes and requires full re-gating — deferred to a future keeper cycle. Per rule #1, no fitted adder applied.

C3b price duration shape 2024: NRMSE 0.202 (0.002 above 0.20 threshold). Investigated lowering ercot_dam_as_scarcity_threshold from 150 to close the gap. Quantitative analysis: the additional overlay hours (37 hours at threshold=100, 77 at threshold=75) fall predominantly in Jan and May, where the model already over-predicts monthly prices vs RT by +$12.69 and +$7.95 respectively. Lowering threshold INCREASES NRMSE: 0.206 at threshold=125, 0.212 at threshold=100, 0.226 at threshold=75. The model's over-prediction in the scarcity months is the binding constraint — more overlay amplifies it. The 0.002 gap is structural LP-dual price-distribution compression; closable only with in-LP energy+AS co-optimization.

C5c storage dispatch shape 2024: r=0.000. EIA-930 battery series coverage is only 19% of hours for 2024 — insufficient for shape correlation. Model dispatches storage economically via daily cycling with vintage ramp and battery_dispatch_adder=10; the benchmark data is too sparse to score shape.

C5c storage dispatch shape 2025: r=0.000. Model storage dispatch follows energy-arbitrage windows but real ERCOT storage cycles primarily for ancillary services (~85% of battery revenue is AS), producing a different monthly profile. Closable only with in-LP AS dispatch co-optimization — a large structural addition for a soft criterion with zero forward-year benefit. Accepted as structural caveat.
